card.title: HUMBER Mk IV
card.flavorText: The Humber Mk IV was a British armored car used extensively during WWII. The Humber was manufactured by the Rootes Group, and the Mk IV variant was the final and most developed version of the Humber series, following the Mk I, Mk II, and Mk III. It was introduced in 1943 and featured several improvements based on the earlier models’ performance in combat. It was fitted with the US M5 or M6 37 mm high-velocity gun, which replaced the earlier 15 mm Besa machine gun. Because the larger gun took up more space, the third crew member located in the turret, the wireless operator, was removed. The turret hatches were also rearranged to accommodate the new gun and crew setup. Around 2,000 units of the Mk IV were produced and it saw widespread use by British and Commonwealth forces, particularly in reconnaissance roles, but also in infantry support roles.
